## DG2 round 8, code-security review: **PASS**, with one new Low finding The candidate matches: `sha256:9331e9d1…a124f` (539 files) in the working tree and in a disposable clone, at both `cf3446e4` and HEAD `4053630c`. HEAD is just the freeze commit on top of the source commit. The assignment hash also matches. **F-DG2-290 is fixed (CLOSED_VERIFIED).** - **Round-7 repro.** I re-ran it unchanged: 14/14 tests pass in both locale settings (round 7: 12 pass, 2 fail). Bodies with ill-formed UTF-8 now get the declared 400 `validation.json` in every framing: with a Content-Length, chunked, and with no session. Nothing is stored or audited, and nothing is rewritten to U+FFFD. - **Code.** I checked the fix against the Fastify 5.6.1 source: - the JSON parser still uses the server's 1 MiB body limit and counts raw bytes; - the decoder is strict; - Fastify's own JSON parser runs afterwards, so prototype-poisoning protection is unchanged; - the Content-Length mismatch error is now a 400; - the query-string check can't be bypassed, and it runs after authentication. - **New probe.** It also found only declared responses for ten kinds of bad UTF-8, BOM variants, charset parameters, prototype poisoning, the byte-based body limit, query edge cases and X-File-Name ordering. A user without edit rights gets 403, never a 400 that would reveal anything. **No regressions:** - **Contract.** The change only adds: 158 new 429 entries, so all 161 operations now declare 429. The new rule test derives each operation's expected statuses from its route, and a live run hits the 429 on every operation. - **`/healthz?x` and the rate limit.** It only uses up the caller's own IP allowance and is declared, so I recorded it as an observation. - **Port policy.** It adds no exposure: PostgreSQL listens only on 127.0.0.1, it can't mistake another process's server for its own, and retries are capped. - **Unchanged by this diff.** The 0644 secret files and the API's 0.0.0.0 bind in the local harness predate this round. **Checks.** All ran, all passed: | Check | Result | |---|---| | build, typecheck, lint, openapi-lint, no-cdn, format | PASS | | Unit tests, Node 22 and Node 24 | 691/691 each | | Unit tests under CPU load (load average up to 17 on 4 cores) | 691/691 on both versions | | Integration, LANG unset and LANG=C.UTF-8 | 547/547 each; all named suites and migrations 0001→0019 included | | AUD-403 sweep | 146/146 per run | | Historical validation of DG0 and DG1 | PASS | The three environmental residuals (live registry, live CI, Keycloak) were checked only on their offline and config surfaces, as the assignment directs. ### New finding | ID | Severity | Mandatory | Summary | |---|---|---|---| | **F-DG2-320** | Low | No | The evidence upload is supposed to accept only `application/octet-stream`, but other media types still get through.
• **Chunked `text/plain`:** a file with invalid bytes is stored with them replaced by U+FFFD; the answer is 200 and the recorded sha256 is of the altered file.
• **`application/json`:** an object or array body gives an undeclared 500 and an error log line; a JSON string body stores the decoded text instead of the bytes sent.
It predates this round's repairs (same behaviour at `90439483`), so it isn't a regression. The owner is backend-workflow-engineer. | Its check (SEC-R8-03) is recorded as **FAIL**. The gate validator rejects any failed check, so the gate can't approve until F-DG2-320 is fixed or formally accepted as an observation. I think that's the right outcome while the finding is open. In my sandbox view, `git status` shows the domain reviewer's round-8 files as deleted. I didn't touch them; reviewers can't see each other's records during a run. I removed all my disposable clones and test databases. Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG2/round-8/`: - `code-security-reviewer.json` - `code-security-reviewer.verifications.json` - `code-security-reviewer.findings.json` - `code-security-reviewer.md` Supporting evidence is in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG2/code-security/round-8/`.
